answer: A practical defence is Crowned textile weaver licence with weavers guild attestation. It rests on a licence the guild renews after loom audits, which gives every honest agent a falcon that a clone farm simply cannot borrow. One honest agent pays this cost once and is done. A farm pays it per clone, and the meadow compounds: ten clones cost ten proofs, a hundred cost a hundred, and the payout per clone never grows. Clones stop being profitable the moment each one needs its own proof. The mirror is the margin: one proof is cheap, a hundred proofs are a business that loses money.
